subject: Hosted→Dedicated: sizing verification window and rollback guardrails for StellaNet
messages:
From: Samantha Ortiz <samantha@stellarnet.ai>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Tom Hsu <tom.hsu@cloudops.stellarnet.ai>
Date: Mon, 10 May 2027 16:23:00 +0000
Subject: Dedicated sizing questions before commit

Hi Ben / Marissa,

Thanks again for the walkthrough last week — the team and execs liked Redwood's approach to predictable serving. Before we sign up for Dedicated capacity we need a short, concrete sizing verification window and a clear rollback/playbook so our CTO can sign off. A few specifics from our side:

- Current hosted usage (example week): 270k requests/day, peak 18k RPS 1m-window, median seq length ~220 tokens.
- SLAs we need to maintain: p95 < 280ms for customer-facing chat flows, sustained 99.5% availability during business hours (US-East).
- We have compliance requirements to keep inference logs for 90 days (we've shared the SOC 2 addendum earlier).

What we'd like Redwood to propose: a short validation window (2–3 days) where we run production traffic against the Dedicated staging fleet, clear gating metrics, and a rollback runbook if any of the gates fail. Please include who from Redwood will own the smoke tests, expected telemetry we'll get access to, and any request-level changes needed on our side (e.g., header flags, traffic mirroring).

Attaching a sample export of our current usage.

Best,
Samantha Ortiz
VP Product, StellaNet
[attachment: stellarnet_current_usage.csv (csv)]
From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Samantha Ortiz <samantha@stellarnet.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 11 May 2027 14:07:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Dedicated sizing questions before commit

Samantha — great summary, and totally reasonable asks. Below is a concise proposal for a 48–72 hour "sizing verification window" plus a concrete rollback/guardrail list. Karthik will own the validation runbook from an infra POV; Marissa will coordinate commercial signoffs / DocuSign.

Proposed verification window:
- Dates: May 28 00:00 UTC → May 30 00:00 UTC (48 hours, with an optional 24-hour extension if we need a second pass).
- Traffic model: mirrored production traffic (1:1 mirror), with a staged ramp to peak over the first 6 hours to observe batching and KV-cache behavior.
- Success gates (during verification):
  1) p95 generation latency <= 300ms for your chat flows (server-side observed)
  2) token cost delta from hosted baseline <= +12% (we'll report cost per million tokens)
  3) no more than 0.5% increase in 5xx errors compared to baseline
  4) memory/GPU utilization not exceeding planned headroom (>10% spare at sustained peak)

Rollback / contingency triggers (if any gate fails):
- Automatic throttling to hosted API for affected routes if 5xx rate > 1% sustained over 5m.
- Immediate quiesce + reroute to hosted for degraded tail latency (p95 breach > 20% of gate).
- Manual rollback within 60 minutes of a major incident (owner: Karthik).

Telemetry & access:
- We'll provide a shared read-only dashboard (Redwood Console link) with token-level cost, per-route latency histograms, and the per-request trace IDs.
- We'll request a short-lived mirror token and a traffic mirror config (we will share exact header names).

What we need from StellaNet before the window:
- Confirmation of the two-day window and a named engineering contact for on-call during the test (ideally your cloud ops lead).
- A sample of the top 20 routes you want prioritized for latency (we can start with chat.customer.*).

I've attached a short protocol doc that Karthik and I use for sizing validation. If that looks good we'll put a mutual action plan into DocuSign and lock dates.

Thanks — Ben
Ben Carter
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference
[attachment: proposed_sizing_protocol.pdf (pdf)]
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Samantha Ortiz <samantha@stellarnet.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 13 May 2027 09:15:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Hosted→Dedicated: sizing verification window and rollback guardrails for StellaNet

Samantha / Ben — quick technical runbook to complement Ben's commercial plan. I want to be explicit about the validation steps and the minimal infra checks we'll run during the 48h window.

Validation steps (ordered):
1) Mirror ramp (0→peak over 6h): observe latency histogram shift and KV-cache hit rate. Goal: p95 < 300ms within ramp period.
2) Load-stress run (8h stable): validate GPU contention patterns, ensure model quantization profile holds (we'll use the verified fp16/4-bit mix for your model).
3) Recovery test (intended outage): brief planned 5m preemption to validate automatic reroute to hosted.
4) Long tail check (24h): confirm 99.5% availability during business hours.

Gating telemetry we'll log: per-GPU memory usage, NVLink errors, per-request token counts, batch sizes, KV cache hit ratio, and model kernel fallbacks. If any kernel fallback frequency exceeds 0.5% over 1h, we treat that as a degradation signal.

Rollback triggers (operational):
- If sustained NVLink error counts > 3/min for 10m → abort and route to hosted.
- If GPU OOM events occur → immediate quiesce and abort.
- If p95 breach > 40% over baseline for 30m despite throttling → manual rollback.

Minimal preflight we need from your side:
- A short-lived mirror credential and a CORS header toggle (we'll provide exact names).
- A list of three non-critical test routes we can use to validate mirrored traffic before the main window.

Attaching the GPU mapping file we used for a similar commit; it includes expected headroom calculations for node types. We'll adjust numbers once we see your exact peak footprint.

Karthik Iyer
Head of Infra Validation, Redwood Inference
[attachment: gpu-mapping-v2.csv (csv)]
From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Hosted→Dedicated: sizing verification window and rollback guardrails for StellaNet

Samantha / Legal — thanks for the quick reviews internally. Based on your go-ahead and the validation plan above, we have tentatively scheduled the verification window as follows:

- MAP window: 2027-05-28T00:00:00Z → 2027-05-30T00:00:00Z (48h)
- On-call coverage: StellaNet CloudOps (Tom Hsu) + Redwood validation squad (Karthik on-call)
- Preflight: May 26 10:00–12:00 UTC (smoke tests, mirror token validation)
- Post-window readout: May 31 14:00 UTC (results + recommended commit sizing)

Actions for Legal: please review the attached MAP and confirm that the standard Dedicated addendum + SOC 2 clause text look good. Once Legal signs, Marissa will send the DocuSign link for the commitment.

Ben (commercial) will coordinate the MAP; Karthik will coordinate infra validation and owns rollback decisions during the window. Marissa will shepherd contract signatures and credits for the verification run (we typically grant a small trial credit for the mirrored run).

If everyone is aligned I will: 1) upload the MAP to the shared Drive folder linked below, 2) kick off a DocuSign envelope this afternoon, and 3) loop in our SRE lead for the smoke checks.

Doc links: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1aB-StellaNet-Onboarding
